# agentgateway_mcp_target (Resource)

Manages an agentgateway MCP target (`mcp.target`). Exactly one transport (`mcp`, `sse`, `stdio` or `openapi`) is required. The resource id is the target `name`; renaming updates in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A streamable HTTP MCP target reached by host, port and path. Exactly one of
# `mcp`, `sse`, `stdio` or `openapi` must be set. `name` is the resource id, so
# renaming updates in place; tools are prefixed with it when multiplexing.
resource "agentgateway_mcp_target" "docs" {
  name      = "docs"
  condition = "request.headers[\"x-tenant\"] == \"acme\""

  mcp = {
    host = "mcp.example.com"
    port = 8080
    path = "/mcp"
  }

  # Transport policies for reaching the backend, as JSON. Not supported on
  # stdio targets.
  policies_json = jsonencode({
    cors = {
      allowOrigins = ["https://app.example.com"]
    }
  })
}

# The same transport can reference a backend defined in the gateway config
# instead of spelling out host and port. `host` and `backend` never combine.
resource "agentgateway_mcp_target" "files" {
  name = "files"

  mcp = {
    backend = "files-backend"
    path    = "/mcp"
  }
}

# An SSE target, using the same host/backend shape.
resource "agentgateway_mcp_target" "events" {
  name = "events"

  sse = {
    host = "https://events.example.com"
    path = "/sse"
  }
}

# A local process target. `clear_env` starts the process with an empty
# environment, so only `env` reaches it.
resource "agentgateway_mcp_target" "local" {
  name = "local"

  stdio = {
    cmd       = "npx"
    args      = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/srv/data"]
    env       = { LOG_LEVEL = "info" }
    clear_env = false
  }
}

# An OpenAPI target: every operation in the schema becomes an MCP tool. The
# gateway accepts the schema as a URL, a file path, or an inline document, and
# requires one; `schema_json` is a JSON leaf, so it is omitted from the payload
# when unset.
resource "agentgateway_mcp_target" "weather" {
  name = "weather"

  openapi = {
    host = "api.example.com"
    port = 443
    path = "/openapi.json"

    schema_json = jsonencode({
      url = "https://api.example.com/openapi.json"
    })
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Target name, which is also the resource id. Used to prefix tool names when multiplexing.

### Optional

- `condition` (String) Boolean CEL expression that selects this target. Omit to always include the target. Conditions require at least two configured targets.
- `mcp` (Attributes) Streamable HTTP transport. Set either `host` (with an optional `port` and `path`) or `backend` (with an optional `path`), never both. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mcp))
- `openapi` (Attributes) OpenAPI transport: the operations in an OpenAPI schema are exposed as MCP tools. Set either `host` (with an optional `port` and `path`) or `backend` (with an optional `path`), never both. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--openapi))
- `policies_json` (String, Sensitive) Transport policies for connecting to the target's backend, as JSON. Not supported on stdio targets. Marked sensitive because `backendAuth` carries credentials.
- `sse` (Attributes) Server-Sent Events transport. Set either `host` (with an optional `port` and `path`) or `backend` (with an optional `path`), never both. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sse))
- `stdio` (Attributes) stdio transport, which starts a local process. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--stdio))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Target id as stored by the gateway (the `name`).
- `revision` (Number) Server revision of the target.

<a id="nestedatt--mcp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mcp`

Optional:

- `backend` (String) Name of a backend defined in the gateway configuration. Conflicts with `host` and `port`.
- `host` (String) Hostname, IP address or full URI of the MCP server, for example `https://example.com` or `example.com:443`. Use only `host` to pass a full URI.
- `path` (String) Request path on the MCP server.
- `port` (Number) Port on the MCP server. Only valid with `host`; the `backend` form has no port.


<a id="nestedatt--openapi"></a>
### Nested Schema for `openapi`

Optional:

- `backend` (String) Name of a backend defined in the gateway configuration. Conflicts with `host` and `port`.
- `host` (String) Hostname, IP address or full URI of the MCP server, for example `https://example.com` or `example.com:443`. Use only `host` to pass a full URI.
- `path` (String) Request path on the MCP server.
- `port` (Number) Port on the MCP server. Only valid with `host`; the `backend` form has no port.
- `schema_json` (String) OpenAPI schema, as JSON: an inline document string (`jsonencode("openapi: 3.0.0...")`), `{url = "https://..."}`, or `{file = "/etc/agentgateway/openapi.json"}`. The gateway requires a schema for an `openapi` target.


<a id="nestedatt--sse"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sse`

Optional:

- `backend` (String) Name of a backend defined in the gateway configuration. Conflicts with `host` and `port`.
- `host` (String) Hostname, IP address or full URI of the MCP server, for example `https://example.com` or `example.com:443`. Use only `host` to pass a full URI.
- `path` (String) Request path on the MCP server.
- `port` (Number) Port on the MCP server. Only valid with `host`; the `backend` form has no port.


<a id="nestedatt--stdio"></a>
### Nested Schema for `stdio`

Required:

- `cmd` (String) Command to start the MCP server.

Optional:

- `args` (List of String) Arguments passed to `cmd`.
- `clear_env` (Boolean) When true, the process inherits no environment variables from the gateway.
- `env` (Map of String, Sensitive) Environment variables passed to the process. Marked sensitive because environment variables routinely carry credentials.
